newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Iran's Velayati says Kazakh oil swaps to continue.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Velayati says Kazakh oil swaps to continue.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Friday his country planned to continue with a stalled two-million-tonne oil swap with the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.
"After solving some minor technical questions, we will continue cooperation in this field," Velayati told reporters after meeting Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev in the Kazakh capital Almaty.

Late on Thursday, Russia's Interfax news agency cited Kazakh oil sources as saying negotiations between the two countries in Kazakhstan's Caspian Sea port of Aktau this week to get the swap restarted were "without result".

The swap, an annual two million tonnes with volumes planned to rise to an eventual six million tonnes, is grounded on mercaptans (sulphur impurities) in Kazakh oil, which the Kazakhs say the Iranians cannot deal with.
About 70,000 tonnes of oil were shipped earlier this year in a trial run from Aktau to Iran's Caspian Sea coast.
Iran had planned to refine initially 40,000 barrels per day of Kazakh crude blended with Iran Light crude. Iran would make the equivalent amount of crude available to Kazakh clients on the Gulf.
"It is not so important how much oil has been transported but that work has started," Velayati said.

Landlocked Kazakhstan, rich in oil and gas, is keen to break its almost total dependence on Russian pipelines to the north for exporting its crude to world markets. Iran wants to play a greater role in the Central Asia region.
